Consider the picture above. Given that $c=a+\lambda b,$ find $\lambda .$
question.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=a+\lambda b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $a.$ So, we begin with the vector $a,$ and then find the remaining vector needed to reach the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251995/assets/4797ffa54b3c2e4d177a6c3d527b1aaf3f1460d3c509bca86395e5f360314d25.png)

Note that in $△OAC,$ we have:

- $AC=3|b|$

- $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $b$ have the same direction

Hence, $\overset{\to }{AC}=3b.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AC} \\  & =a+3b.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=a+\lambda b=a+3b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $b,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =3
$$
